artworks.title: Rhea Handing a Swaddled Stone to Cronus
artworks.description: Met pelike: Rhea offers Cronus the wrapped stone in place of the infant — the trick that lets Zeus survive the Titan's swallowings.

artworks.title: Rhea Presenting Cronus the Stone Wrapped in Cloth
artworks.description: Nineteenth-century wood engraving of the birth's hinge: Rhea delivers the swaddled rock while the true child is hidden for Crete.

artworks.title: The Childhood of Zeus
artworks.description: Jordaens' Louvre canvas: the infant Jupiter among Corybantes and the goat Amalthea — Cretan nurture after Rhea's deceit.

artworks.title: The Infant Jupiter Fed by the Goat Amalthea
artworks.description: Louvre nursing scene: Amalthea feeds the hidden thunderer — the Cretan childhood that will end Cronus' reign.

artworks.title: The Infancy of Zeus
artworks.description: Watts' Symbolist infancy: the future king of the gods as a child in the mountain cave — birth myth as Victorian allegory of power waiting.

popCulture.title: Zeus
popCulture.description: The Cretan cave and the stone Cronus swallowed remain the birth that ends the Titan reign — Rhea's trick and the thunderer's childhood.
